best_fit_when: Buyer has repeated manual intake, follow-up, reporting, or handoff work and the builder can deliver a concrete workflow
minimum_evidence: One before-after workflow example plus 10 targeted buyer replies or one paid pilot request
primary_page_asset: One-page service page with workflow screenshot, scope, delivery time, limits, and intake CTA
paid_offer_shape: Fixed-scope setup or review before larger implementation
common_stop_rule: Stop if buyers cannot name the workflow pain or if delivery needs private account takeover

best_fit_when: Buyer has existing process or website but does not know what to automate first
minimum_evidence: Public site/process sample, tool stack, risk boundary, and audit decision question
primary_page_asset: Audit sample, checklist, scope builder, and decision table
common_stop_rule: Stop if the buyer expects implementation, guaranteed savings, or regulated advice

best_fit_when: Buyer repeats a narrow task and needs reusable assets, not custom service
minimum_evidence: Three task examples, one sample output, and clear buyer role
primary_page_asset: Template preview page with examples, use cases, and refund boundary
paid_offer_shape: Low-price downloadable pack or starter bundle
common_stop_rule: Stop if generic AI can produce equivalent output without domain constraints

best_fit_when: Buyer repeats a task often enough to justify software and the builder can maintain it
minimum_evidence: Manual workflow proof, repeated demand, and support capacity
primary_page_asset: Tool page with free checker, output sample, and upgrade boundary
paid_offer_shape: Free tool plus paid export, setup, or pro workflow
common_stop_rule: Stop if the task is rare, data rights are unclear, or support cost exceeds price

route_archetype: SEO or AI visibility guide cluster
best_fit_when: The problem is education and reference demand rather than direct service buying
minimum_evidence: Source pack, search intent, internal linking plan, and update owner
primary_page_asset: Guide hub with checklists, source register, and review cycle
paid_offer_shape: Newsletter, templates, audit, or consulting only after traffic evidence
common_stop_rule: Stop if pages repeat public advice without original tool, data, or checklist value

best_fit_when: Entities can be collected legally and each page has unique value
minimum_evidence: Data rights, canonical entity model, uniqueness field, and sample audit
primary_page_asset: Directory template, filters, schema, and noindex rules
paid_offer_shape: Sponsorship, lead gen, or paid placement only after demand proof
common_stop_rule: Stop if data is copied, thin, stale, or impossible to maintain

best_fit_when: Buyer is choosing between methods, tools, or service types and needs tradeoffs
minimum_evidence: Current source pack, benchmark criteria, update date, and bias disclosure
primary_page_asset: Comparison matrix with use cases, limits, and source notes
paid_offer_shape: Affiliate, audit, or advisory path with disclosure
common_stop_rule: Stop if pricing/spec claims cannot be verified from current sources

best_fit_when: Buyer needs implementation more than advice and has one offer already
minimum_evidence: Offer input, proof asset, brand basics, payment/intake boundary, and delivery capacity
primary_page_asset: Service page with sample before-after page structure
paid_offer_shape: Fixed-price setup with clear revision and scope limits
common_stop_rule: Stop if the buyer expects broad strategy, design system, or traffic guarantees

best_fit_when: Buyer has first-party data and needs decisions from it
minimum_evidence: Clean data export, metric definition, privacy boundary, and decision question
primary_page_asset: Report sample, KPI glossary, and data handling note
common_stop_rule: Stop if data is unavailable, sensitive, or the decision cannot be changed by analysis

best_fit_when: The task happens in a browser repeatedly and has a narrow trigger
minimum_evidence: Manual task proof, target browser context, permissions review, and maintenance plan
primary_page_asset: Demo page with permission explanation and workflow screenshots
paid_offer_shape: Free extension plus paid setup/support only after usage proof
common_stop_rule: Stop if permissions are excessive or the task can be solved with a bookmark/template

best_fit_when: Buyer wants a repeatable process and can execute without custom service
minimum_evidence: Clear learner level, one sample module, proof of outcome, and support boundary
primary_page_asset: Curriculum page with module sample and action checklist
paid_offer_shape: One-time playbook or cohort only after audience proof
common_stop_rule: Stop if the material is generic or lacks practice assets

best_fit_when: Two sides have repeated demand and the operator can seed supply manually
minimum_evidence: Manual supply list, buyer request proof, trust/safety rules, and matching workflow
primary_page_asset: Request page with qualification rules and trust boundaries
paid_offer_shape: Manual concierge matching before platform build
common_stop_rule: Stop if either side cannot be sourced manually or trust risk is high
